$schema_note: Maps release artifacts to their Nexus Mods targets. To publish, create a GitHub Release tagged '<artifact>-v<version>' (e.g. mwbf-v1.0.1). The release.yml workflow parses the tag, stages contentDir into installDir, zips it as '<fileBaseName>_v<version>.zip' (so 'r6/...' sits at the zip root), attaches the zip to the release, and uploads to Nexus via Nexus-Mods/upload-action (beta.10, v3 upload API). See the portfolio's RELEASING notes / the nexus-ci-release-pipeline wiki page.
$paths_note: contentDir = repo folder whose CONTENTS ship. installDir = path inside the zip those contents are placed at (the in-game install path under the Cyberpunk 2077 root). fileBaseName = the download filename stem (version is appended). Pure redscript - loose .reds files under r6/scripts/MapWaypointBugFixes, no WolvenKit packing.
$contentdir_note: contentDir is 'r6' so the zip root is 'r6/scripts/MapWaypointBugFixes/*.reds'. The mod ships nothing outside r6/scripts.
$file_id_note: The Nexus file id is NOT stored here. It lives in a REPOSITORY VARIABLE named NEXUS_FILE_ID_MWBF (the artifact key 'mwbf' uppercased, '-' -> '_'), set under Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions > Variables. A file_id DOES NOT EXIST until the mod's first file has been uploaded to Nexus BY HAND, so committing a placeholder commits a lie. Get it from the mod page's Files tab > 'API Info' (Nexus labels it 'Group ID'). DO NOT use the file_id from the public v1 API -- that is a different id space and the wrong value looks entirely plausible.
$mod_page_note: Two keys here drive the mod PAGE rather than the file. `update_mod_version` sets the page's headline version to the released file's version: true for a mod's own main artifact, false for any artifact that shares a page with another (an SLM preset would otherwise stamp '1.0.0kp' onto the page). `nexus_mod_id` is the number in the mod page URL; the workflow looks it up at release time to get the internal id the changelog endpoint needs, so a wrong number here costs the changelog and never posts it to the wrong page. The page DESCRIPTION is still manual -- no endpoint in the pipeline touches it.
